Simulacra is honestly a very creative horror game, I haven't seen anything quite like it. I really love the story. The gameplay is fantastic and I loved going through Anna's phone and slowly putting the puzzle together about what happened. Great game!
I wouldn't really call this "horror". Some jumpscares I guess but nothing major. I thought it was good as a mystery game, there is replayability if you want to try different methods.

Length <3hrs

Simulacra is a Mystery game in which the player is in possession of a missing girl's phone. Using the contacts and apps on her phone you need to track down what happened to her.

Using her phone you will be looking through her life, personal messages and contracts. This will expose you to her life, how she interacted with her friends and colleagues, and what led up to her losing her phone. The transitions of the phone's main image really works well for bringing the horror into the exploration, while the missing information on her phone adds to the mystery between the events.

The puzzles were straight forward, as information I needed to access further parts of the phone easily stood out to me from when I read through her texts and messages. This helped from needing to search through every part of the phone for something I missed.

In all aspects Simulacra feels like a refinement of ‘Sara is Missing’. The texts are not as large and information felt like it was a lot simpler to find, making the game much more enjoyable to get through.

Overall I really enjoyed Simulacra, it may have what feels like weak acting and some moments of absurdity. Yet the character development is great, and looking back on her life and what led up to the moments, with the mystery behind the dating app really made the game intriguing.

I am a bit middling on this game, I'd rate it 3 stars if I could. It involves a lot of reading so if you are going to stream it, bring a gallon of water. Some of the plot points feel hackneyed and some communications feel forced. However, the game builds to a great (few) endings, which will make you come back for more. By the end, I was excited to play the second one.

I casually started playing this at 11pm planning on going to bed in not long, but I found myself too immersed and stayed up until 3am to finish it! I don't know if I will replay it for different achievements but this was definitely an unforgettable experience. I highly recommend playing with earphones as well, makes for a creepier atmosphere. I'm not usually into narrative games, but this did a great job at mixing texting with the gradual unlocking of more content, as well as doing "stalker" work and putting your observation skills to the test in order to solve the mystery.

SIMULACRA is a short, but awesome indie/horror game with the neat concept of all the action taking place on a missing woman's phone that you interact with. Even though you can get through the game at a pretty solid pace, there's still a lot to take in and a whole to enjoy. The best thing about it of course is that your choices do matter and will dictate what ending you get. So yes, this is an indie game well worth picking up.
